# Status

`c.Status` calls the API's Status group. The status summary of a node.

## Methods

| Method                       | Returns                              | Permission    | Description                         |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| [`Get(ctx, hostname)`](#get) | `*Response[Collection[StatusEntry]]` | `status:read` | Get the status summary of the host. |

### Get

```go
func (s *StatusService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[StatusEntry]], error)
```

Get the status summary of the host.

Runs the get of the hostname, uptime, os, load, memory and disk behaviors on the
host, and answers with each. A read that fails is in errors, as its name and its
error, and the other fields still answer.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/status`, and needs the permission
`status:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

An Ubuntu host, `go run status.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.Status.Get(ctx, target)
```

### RowStatus

What happened on the host: ok, the operation ran and succeeded; failed, it ran
and did not succeed; skipped, the host's OS family does not support it; timeout,
the host did not answer, so nobody knows whether it ran.

A `string`, one of `ok`, `failed`, `skipped`, `timeout`.
